findings.evidence:
src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:751 `
${esc(it.display_text ?? it.text)}
` and :755 `${(it.display_text ?? it.text).length...}` are the only consumers of `display_text`. `grep -rn display_text src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py evals/golden evals/adversarial` returns only server-side payload assertions plus one triage sentence - nothing binds index.html to the key. ORCHESTRATOR RE-RAN INDEPENDENTLY: invariant 36/36 = 1.000, fast 78/78 = 1.000, both fully green with the pane showing un-stripped text under a 'boilerplate hidden' header.

findings.claim: The rewritten `check_boilerplate_plumbing` binds the NAMES on the wire but only checks the flag's VALUE at one of the two value-carrying hops, so five realistic breakages against the real files still return 0 failures - two of which invert default-OFF into always-exclude, the same headline-requirement class R2 was raised for.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:699-717: `read = set(re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', expr))` compares only quoted literals, so any operator/inversion in the handler expression is invisible; the only value-integrity assertion is :731-735, the `_run` -> `extract_items` hop. Measured against copies of the real app.py + index.html at 39dfa2c, all returning 0 failures (control 0): M1 fixture handler `exclude_boilerplate=not bool((body or {}).get("exclude_boilerplate"))` (fixture-dropdown mode inverted - default OFF now excludes); M2 upload handler `!= "1"` instead of `== "1"` (one-character typo; with the box unticked the query param is absent, `None != "1"` is True, so EVERY upload excludes - and upload is the no-network path an evaluator uses); M3 `exclude_boilerplate=False and bool(...)` (fixture mode never excludes); M4 `function excludeBp(){ return true; }` (helper ignores the checkbox - R2 shape (b) relocated one level up, and the docstring at :657-659 claims to require call sites to 'read excludeBp() rather than a constant', which M4 satisfies while severing all three modes); M5 `$("#exclude-bp-OLD")` inside excludeBp (helper always false - the checkbox never excludes anything).
findings.repro: Copy app.py and index.html to a scratch dir, apply each of M1-M5, call check_boilerplate_plumbing against the copies - all five return []. ORCHESTRATOR RE-RAN M2 INDEPENDENTLY: 0 failures, [].
findings.acceptance: The check asserts each handler forwards the read value unmodified (no `not`/`!=`/constant between the request read and the `exclude_boilerplate=` kwarg) and that `excludeBp()`'s body actually reads `#exclude-bp`'s `.checked`; M1-M5 are added to the fixture pair at the new exact count and each is watched red individually before being claimed covered.

findings.claim: The new regression case's triage note states a rationale for the exact count that is factually false: it claims a blanket-failing check 'would exceed the pinned count rather than reach it', but an always-firing wire comparison hits exactly 5 on the fixture pair, because no endpoint in the pair reaches the comparison and agrees.
findings.evidence: evals/adversarial/ui-boilerplate-exclusion-regression.json triage.note. In the fixture pair the fixture endpoint fails at the UI branch (so `sent` stays None and the comparison is never reached), and url + upload both disagree - there is no agreeing pair for the comparison to be tested on. Measured: mutating eval_adapter.py:709 `if sent is not None and sent != read:` to `if sent is not None and True:` gives exactly 5 failures with the same 5 messages, i.e. the case stays PASS. The mutation IS caught, but by the OTHER half of the pair (ui-boilerplate-exclusion on the real files goes FAIL, invariant 35/36 = 0.972) - not by the exact count the note credits.
findings.repro: Apply the `sent != read` -> `True` mutation, run the fixture-pair check -> 5 failures, regression case PASS; invariant -> ui-boilerplate-exclusion FAIL, 35/36.
findings.acceptance: Either the triage note is corrected to credit the green half of the pair for the over-fire direction, or the fixture pair adds one endpoint where both ends agree so the exact count itself distinguishes a correct comparison from an always-firing one.

findings.claim: The R1 fix serialises the item body twice for every item that contains any chrome, roughly doubling the ON-path payload, and nothing in the diff, the resolution or the TODO row discloses the cost.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/view.py:62-63 emits `display_text` in addition to the (now always verbatim) `text`, both truncated at DISPLAY_MAX=40,000. Measured over the committed fixtures, `len(json.dumps(build_view(...)))` OFF -> ON: cat-2023 222,559 -> 428,434 (+205,875); nvda-2024 196,474 -> 376,530; heading-unnumbered 196,598 -> 376,859; msft-2013 201,641 -> 379,914; ge-1994 85,548 -> 161,045. 21 of 38 fixtures grow by more than 20 KB. Separately, `display_text` is emitted whenever `body != raw` even if the difference falls beyond DISPLAY_MAX, in which case it is byte-identical to `text`; the check's dead-payload guard only fires when NOTHING was stripped, so that redundancy is unpinned (0 such items on today's fixtures, so no live symptom).
findings.repro: For each fixture: json.dumps(build_view(extract_items(f))) vs the same with exclude_boilerplate=True.
findings.acceptance: Either emit only one body (e.g. send `display_text` and keep the anchor oracle's needle server-side) or record the doubling in the S8 row / a debt row as a knowingly accepted cost, with the measured numbers.

findings.claim: The rejection rationale for the HTTP option is written as 'evals/run.py has no skip state', but run.py does have an unscored case state - the `debt` suite - which is excluded from both `score` and `is_red`; the load-bearing half of the argument (three CI jobs install nothing) is verified true, so the conclusion stands but the stated fact does not.
findings.evidence: evals/run.py:141-147 separates the debt set, :148-150 `score = passed / len(results)` over the non-debt set only, and :166 `is_red` also excludes debt_results - four cases already use it. The claim appears verbatim in src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:664-668, tasks/TODO.md's corrected debt row, tasks/reviews/pr27-r1-resolution.json and prompts/012. VERIFIED TRUE in the same run: requirements.txt lists fastapi+uvicorn but not httpx; ci.yml has exactly three jobs and none runs `pip install`; `import fastapi` fails in this environment. So the conclusion is sound; the premise as written is not, and `debt` is a poor fit anyway (a dep-missing case would read as 'STILL RED' in CI and 'NOW GREEN - promote it' locally).
findings.repro: sed -n 135,170p evals/run.py; grep -rn '"debt"' evals/adversarial; grep -n 'pip install' .github/workflows/ci.yml
findings.acceptance: The three copies of the sentence say what is actually true - that run.py's only unscored state is the `debt` suite, which is semantically 'known-red limitation' and would misreport a dependency-conditional case in both directions - rather than 'no skip state'.
